2103:

2132:
** εὐνο-έω**,
**to be well-inclined** or **favourable**, with _dative_, τοῖσι ἐμοῖσι πρήγμασι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.237}}; τινι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 689, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1411, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 12.5, etc.; ὀμνύω.. εὐνοήσειν Καίσαρι “OGI” 532.9 (Galatia, Aug.); τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ}}**be at peace with,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|NT.Matt.5.25: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.79}}; ὁ εὐνοῶν one's **well-wisher**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Eudemia” 1241a11}}:—_middle_, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd-2nd c.BC: Phalaris Epistolographus “Epistulae - Epistolographi” 119}}:—_passive_, **to be kindly** or **affectionately treated**, uncertain reading in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 1087; ὑπὸ γυναικός Vett. Val. 68.3}}; **to be liked**, ὑπὸ θεῶν καὶ ὑπὸ γυναικῶν {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Hephaestio Astrologus 1.1.}}
2134:
** εὐνουχ-ίζω**,

2139:
** εὐπερί-στᾰτος**, ον,

2140:

2144:

(i.e. ὄν) with _infinitive_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.Supp.” p.7S.}}

** εὐρακύλων**, ωνος, ὁ,
name of a north-east wind, = Latin (Vulg.) **euroaquilo**, ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος εὐ. {{NT|NT.Act.27.14}}, with many variants, including **εὐροκλύδων.**
2149:
** εὐρῠχωρ-ος**, ον,
**roomy, wide**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 675b27; πεδίον 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 19.84; ναῦς 1st c.BC(?): Maximus Astrologus Tyr. 1.3}}; τὰ εὐ. **wide spaces**, Aen.{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|Tact. 2.2, 3rd-2nd c.BC: Philo Mechanicus “(Belopoeica) Excerpte aus Philons Mechanik - Ath. Berl. Akad.” 92.47.}}
2151:
** εὐσεβ-έω**,
**live** or **act piously** or **reverently**, _absolutely_, {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 145, “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.8 (_Locrian dialect_, 5th c.BC), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1350, etc.}}; εἴς τινα towards one, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Ant.” 731; περί τινα 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 1148; περὶ θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 193a; πρὸς τὸν θεόν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 567; πρὸς θεούς “Anthologia Graeca” 10.107 (5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus); εὐ. τὰ πρὸς θεούς 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1441; τὰ περὶ τοὺς θεούς 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.2}}; of outward acts of service, θύουσα καὶ εὐσεβοῦσα τοῖς θεοῖς {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|“PRyl.” 112 (a). 4 (3rd c.AD)}}; εὐ. θεούς **to reverence** them, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 338 (nisi to be read εὖ σέβειν); εὐσεβήσασαν τὴν θεόν “BCH” 44.77 (from Lagina):}} —_passive_, εὐσεβεῖσθαι **to be reverenced**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.11, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.201}}; of a duty, **to be reverently discharged**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 364c.}}
2156:
Related to: ** εὐσχημον-έω**,
**to behave with decorum**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 732c, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Μονόστιχοι - Fragmenta Comicorum Graecorum” 646, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.281 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “PSI” 5.541.5.}}

2177:
** ἐφάλλομαι**,
_future_ - αλοῦμαι {{LXX|LXX.1Ki.10.6: _Epic dialect_}}_aorist 2_ ἐπᾶλτο, _participle_ ἐπάλμενος, ἐπιάλμενος (see. below): regular _aorist 2_ _infinitive_ -αλέσθαι {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“IG” 4.951.27 (Epid., 4th c.BC)}}:—**spring upon**, so as to **attack**, with _dative_, Ἀστεροπαίῳ ἐπᾶλτο {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.140, compare 13.643; Τρώεσσιν ἐπάλμενος 11.489, etc.}}; ἐπάλμενος ὀξέϊ δουρί{{Refs 8th c.BC+|[prev. work] 421, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 14.220: without hostile sense, with _genitive_, ἵππων ἐπιάλμενος}} **having leaped upon** the chariot, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.15; κύσσε.. μιν.. ἐπιάλμενος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 24.320}}; of fame, ἐς Αἰθίοπας ἐπᾶλτο {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 6.50: rare in Prose, ἐπὶ τὸν οὐδὸν ἐ. (a Homeric reminiscence) 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ion” 535b}}; ἐπὶ τὰν χῆρα {{NT+1st c.AD+|“IG” [same place]; ἐπί τινας NT.Act.19.16; ἵπποις 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.139b; θαλάττης 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 1.10}}; ζῴῳ, in hostile sense, {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus “de Venenatis Animalibus” 33.3}}; εἰς τοὐπίσω ἐ., of an exercise, {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.145: _metaphorically_, of the spirit of prophecy, LXX [same place]}}

2189:
** ἔχθρ-α**,
_Ionic dialect_ **ἔχθρη**, ἡ, **hatred, enmity**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.81, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.145, etc.}}: in philosophical sense, ={νεῖκος}{{Refs 3rd c.AD+|1.5, 3rd c.AD: Plotinus Philosophus 3.2.2}}; ἔ. τινός **hatred for, enmity to** one, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.1, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.10; κατ᾽ ἔχθραν τινός 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 133; ἔ. ἔς τινα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.5, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68; εἴς θεόν NT.Rom.8.7; πρός τινα 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 491 (_plural_), 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.68}}; δι᾽ ἔχθρας μολεῖν, ἀφῖχθαί τινι, to be **at feud** with one, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 479, “Hipp.” 1164; δι᾽ ἔχθρας οὐδετέρῳ γενήσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1412; εἰς ἔ. βάλλειν τινά 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 390; εἰς ἔ. ἐλθεῖν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.62; καταστῆσαί τινας εἰς ἔχθραν τῷ δήμῳ 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.5.9; πολλὴν εἰς ἔχθραν ἀλλήλοις καὶ πολλῶν πέρι καθίστανται 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 307d, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 9.67}}; πρὸς ἔχθραν from **personal enmity**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.141}}; ἔ. συμβάλλειν, συνάπτειν τινί, to engage in **hostility** with.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 45, “Heracl.” 459; ἔ. τισὶν ἄρασθαι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.132; καταλλάσσεσθαι τὰς ἔ. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.145; λύσασαν ἔ. τὴν πάρος 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 50; τὰς μεγάλας ἔ. διαλύεσθαι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.19; πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἔ. ἀνείλοντο 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.9; διαλλαχθῆναι τῆς ἔ. 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 2.26: proverbial, Ἐμπεδοκλέους ἔ.}}, of undying **hatred**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator “Fragmenta” 261 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus}}
